correctness.rationale: The bracket gives the three centralizer constraints [X,Y]=0, X_V w=Y_V v and omega(v,w)=0, with the last coordinate free. At X=0, the common sl2-annihilator of the columns of v has dimension 3, 1 or 0 in column-span rank 0, 1 or 2; also omega(v,-) has rank one precisely when v is nonzero. For nonzero X in odd characteristic, X is nonscalar, its matrix commutant is spanned by I and X, and taking trace zero gives Y=tX. Thus w=tv+u for u in ker X_V, with omega(v,u)=0. In the nilpotent case the kernel is Lagrangian, so the last condition cuts its dimension by one exactly for v outside it. Each of the q+1 possible kernel lines permits q-1 nonzero maps from the quotient line back to it, giving q²-1 nonzero nilpotents. The invertible case has u=0. These give the six counts, allowing empty or coincident strata. The sum of counts times q to the centralizer dimension is q^(4n+1)+q^(3n+1)(q+1)(q²-1)+q^(2n+2)(q^4+q^3-q²-2q+1); division by q^(4n+8) verifies the exact probability and fixed-q limit. This derivation applies to extension fields as well; the checked support describes finite prime-field examples only. The uploaded checker was not executed.

value.rationale: This is a complete distribution for a natural nonreductive Lie family, not just a finite sample or a count transported from the sl2 quotient. The Lagrangian incidence split changes the centralizer rank for an entire structural stratum. The exact distribution explains why the commuting probability stays positive as the module dimension grows: when both sl2 components vanish only symplectic orthogonality remains, producing the q^-7 limiting contribution. The census quantifies the contribution of the other strata, including the first correction.
